title: Electrical Engineering
summary: A three-year, laboratory-rich route from mathematical foundations to specialization and a defended senior design project.
notice: Independent, non-accredited study. Course Atlas does not award a university degree, transferable credit, or professional licensure.
workload: One internal workload credit represents approximately 40–45 hours of combined study, practice, laboratory, assessment, and project work. It is not an academic credit conversion.
outcomes: Analyze and design electrical, electronic, computational, signal, control, communication, and energy systems.
Build reproducible simulations, laboratory evidence, technical reports, and a public engineering portfolio.
Select one coherent specialization and complete a two-stage capstone with review, verification, and defense.
terms: Semester 1 · Year 1 · See the whole field
Semester 2 · Year 1 · Measure, model, and program
Semester 3 · Year 2 · Build the analog and digital base
Semester 4 · Year 2 · Think in systems and uncertainty
Semester 5 · Year 3 · Choose depth and prove the design
Semester 6 · Year 3 · Integrate, deploy, and defend

courses.title: Calculus I: Models and Change
courses.summary: Limits, derivatives, integrals, approximation, and engineering models taught through physical examples.
courses.first: Take the Single Variable Calculus diagnostic, then complete the first limits lecture and five warm-up problems.
outcomes: Model rates and accumulated quantities, justify a solution, and use calculus confidently in mechanics and circuits.
setup: Create a calculus notebook with one page for definitions, one for worked problems, and one for errors.
Install Python with SciPy or use a browser notebook for numerical checks and plots.

courses.title: Smart Grids & Protection
courses.summary: Work across conversion, machines, grids, protection, storage, and renewable generation at consequential scale. This is an independently versioned Energy & Power course, not a mutable specialization placeholder.
courses.first: Build and solve a three-bus per-unit network, then reconcile every bus power balance.
outcomes: Complete and defend the Smart Grids & Protection technical work defined in this published course version.
setup: Install OpenModelica and create a versioned one-line/network data set with base quantities and scenario definitions.
Use only simulation/public data; document load, generation, protection, and outage assumptions.

units.activity: Create and unit-audit a small network model.

units.activity: Run base-case load flow and explain voltage/loading results.

units.activity: Automate branch/generator outage screening.

units.activity: Calculate and simulate selected bus fault current.

units.activity: Create a selective protection scheme for the model.
